item.title: #3641267: Update Twig to v3.31.1
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 10.6.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +20/−25 · lock +17/−17 · php +2/−7 · json +1/−1
  • Diff: 1dec2b8
  • Discussion: #3641267 · 5 contributors · 34 comments
  • Followers: 6
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

Drupal core now requires and locks Twig 3.31.1 (and twig/html-extra 3.31.1), picking up fixes for newly published Twig CVEs. The update was also committed to the 12.0.x, 11.x, 11.5.x, 11.4.x, 11.3.x and 10.6.x branches. Sites should update to a core release containing it, or otherwise run composer update twig/twig so composer audit stops reporting the advisories.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Security: Updates Twig to v3.31.1 to address newly released Twig CVEs (the issue flags them via composer audit).
  • API change: Core's Twig loader addPath() gains a third parameter bool $check = TRUE on main, matching Twig's FilesystemLoader; subclasses overriding it need a compatible signature.

Technical details

The commit bumps the twig/twig constraint from ^3.28.0 to ^3.31.1 in core's composer.json, and updates composer.lock (twig/twig from v3.30.0 to v3.31.1, twig/html-extra from v3.29.0 to v3.31.1). The issue states lockfiles and core-recommended need the update before further security releases on all supported branches.

Twig 3.31 adds a bool $check argument to FilesystemLoader::addPath(). Core's Twig loader overrides that method, so on main its signature becomes addPath(string $path, string $namespace = self::MAIN_NAMESPACE, bool $check = TRUE): void, and the docblock is replaced with {@inheritdoc}. In the thread, the concern was that making this a required signature change could disrupt contrib or custom subclasses on production branches; for 11.4.x the MR was reworked to use Twig's commented-out parameter form (/* , bool $check = true */) with deprecation ignores, while 11.5.x keeps the new parameter. I only read the main diff, so the exact backport forms on other branches are not verified here.

Upgrade

If you extend the core Twig loader and override addPath(), update the signature on main/12.0.x:

public function addPath(string $path, string $namespace = self::MAIN_NAMESPACE, bool $check = TRUE): void {

Sites using their own lockfile should run composer update twig/twig twig/html-extra.

item.title: #2448545: Modernize form select option helpers
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +126/−60 · php +126/−60
  • Diff: ca18eda
  • Discussion: #2448545 · 48 contributors · 185 comments
  • Followers: 53

Summary

The two remaining option helper functions in form.inc are deprecated. form_select_options() now has a class-based replacement, and form_get_options(), which core does not use, is deprecated with no replacement. Both will be removed in Drupal 13. Contrib and custom code that calls either function will emit deprecation notices.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: form_select_options() deprecated in favour of \Drupal\Core\Form\FormSelectOptions::process(); form_get_options() deprecated with no replacement, both removed in drupal:13.0.0.
  • New API: New final class \Drupal\Core\Form\FormSelectOptions with static process() method.

Technical details

The logic of form_select_options() moved unchanged into the new final class Drupal\Core\Form\FormSelectOptions as FormSelectOptions::process(array $element, $choices = NULL): array. The class has a private constructor and is not meant to be instantiated or extended. The old function now calls trigger_error() with E_USER_DEPRECATED and delegates to process(). Core's own caller, the select preprocess in ElementInfoManager-adjacent theme preprocess code (preprocessSelect()), now calls FormSelectOptions::process() directly. The docblocks were moved as they were, with improvements left to the follow-up #3548829.

form_get_options() only gets a deprecation notice and trigger, with no replacement. One small difference in the moved code: the empty-option check for multiple selects changed from $key == '_none' to $key === '_none'. Since $key is already cast to a string, behaviour should be the same. Replacing the hard-coded '_none' with a constant was split into #3548830. The earlier broader approach, which introduced an options constant, was dropped to reduce scope.

Upgrade

Replace calls to the deprecated function:

// Before.
$options = form_select_options($element);
// After.
use Drupal\Core\Form\FormSelectOptions;
$options = FormSelectOptions::process($element);

form_get_options() has no replacement; stop using it.

item.title: #3249027: RoleAccessCheck returns Allowed if user has no role
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +31/−15 · php +31/−15
  • Diff: 3a0ae0d
  • Discussion: #3249027 · 16 contributors · 59 comments
  • Followers: 18
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 16 contributors

Summary

The _role route access check now explicitly denies access when an account has no roles at all. Core accounts always carry at least the anonymous or authenticated role, so ordinary sites see no change. The guard protects against future changes, such as a different default for getRoles(), or custom account objects that return no roles.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: RoleAccessCheck now returns forbidden for any account with no roles, a defensive guard with no known exploit in current core.

Technical details

\Drupal\user\Access\RoleAccessCheck::access() now calls $account->getRoles() once, and if the result is empty returns AccessResult::forbidden('No user roles found.') before parsing the _role requirement. Previously an empty role list on a _role route fell through to AccessResult::neutral() with the user.roles cache context. The same $roles variable is reused in the array_diff() (comma, AND) and array_intersect() (plus, OR) branches. The forbidden result carries no user.roles cache context.

Because forbidden wins over allowed when access results are combined, an account without roles is now denied outright, where before another access checker could still grant access. The thread established that the bug was not reproducible in current core: an empty array already led to neutral. The change is a guard against future changes. RoleAccessCheckTest gains a $forbidden_accounts data provider argument covering $account_none (empty roles) and $account_null (NULL roles).

item.title: #3437608: Add validation constraints to system.performance
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +466/−19 · php +386/−5 · yml +80/−14
  • Diff: ab043e9
  • Discussion: #3437608 · 11 contributors · 79 comments
  • Followers: 12
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 11 contributors

Summary

The system.performance config is now fully validatable. Page cache max age must be an integer between 0 and 31536000 seconds. When Fast 404 is enabled, its paths and exclude_paths must be valid regular expressions and its html must be a valid HTML document, and all three keys are required. When Fast 404 is disabled, those keys may be omitted, but if present they are still validated. Core also gains reusable Html and ValidRegex constraints and matching schema types that contrib and custom config schemas can use.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: system.performance is now FullyValidatable; cache.page.max_age must be 0 to 31536000, and fast_404 paths, exclude_paths and html are validated and required when fast_404.enabled is true.
  • New API: New Html (mode fragment or document) and ValidRegex validation constraints, and new html_fragment, html_document and regex config schema data types.

Technical details

core.data_types.schema.yml gains three types: regex (constraint ValidRegex), html_fragment (Html with mode: fragment) and html_document (Html with mode: document). The constraints live in Drupal\Core\Validation\Plugin\Validation\Constraint as HtmlConstraint/HtmlConstraintValidator and ValidRegexConstraint/ValidRegexConstraintValidator. They sit in core's Validation namespace rather than a component, to avoid a new dependency from the Utility component. HtmlConstraint throws an InvalidArgumentException for any mode other than fragment or document; the validator parses with Masterminds\HTML5 and adds each parser error as a violation, and ignores NULL. ValidRegexConstraintValidator checks @preg_match($value, "") !== FALSE and reports the preg_last_error_msg() text in the violation.

In system.schema.yml, cache.page.max_age gets a Range of 0 to 31536000, matching PerformanceForm::buildForm(). fast_404 is now a dynamic type system.performance.fast_404.[enabled], resolving to system.performance.fast_404.1 (enabled: paths, exclude_paths, html required) or system.performance.fast_404.0 (disabled: the same keys with requiredKey: false), both extending system.performance.fast_404.*. Consequently, enabling Fast 404 without those keys fails with SchemaIncompleteException on save. Fast404Test and CommandsTest were adjusted accordingly (the latter now calls installConfig(['system'])). Coverage of the HTML validator is questioned in follow-up #3639758.

Upgrade

Custom schemas can reuse the new types:

my_module.settings:
  type: config_object
  mapping:
    pattern:
      type: regex
      label: 'Regular expression'
    page_html:
      type: html_document
      label: 'HTML page'

Code that enables fast_404 in system.performance programmatically must also set paths, exclude_paths and html.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: April 2, 2024
  • Committed: November 24, 2026 (2 years later)

Key contributors

  • phenaproxima (Acquia)
  • narendrar (Acquia)
  • mikelutz (Four Kitchens)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • borisson_ (Calibrate)
  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • bbrala (SWIS)
  • wim leers (Acquia)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)

Collaboration

The scope shifted considerably during review. Early on, max_age was limited to multiples of 60 via DivisibleBy; catch disagreed and it became a plain 0 to 31536000 range, with form UX changes split to #3451592. mikelutz added the ValidRegex constraint and the regex type. alexpott objected to HTML validation depending on a parser from the Utility component, which led mikelutz to move it into a full Html constraint in core's Validation namespace with a fragment/document mode. alexpott also questioned why the schema varies with fast_404.enabled. bbrala traced the pattern to existing examples such as core.date_format.* and editor.image_upload_settings.*, and showed that defining the disabled state too keeps values validated while letting the keys be absent.

item.title: #3638970: Update JavaScript dependencies for 12.0.0
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical task
  • Version: 12.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 10 files, +1382/−1164 · lock +1098/−958 · js +259/−181 · json +16/−16 · yml +8/−8 · map +1/−1
  • Diff: 5776d7d
  • Discussion: #3638970 · 5 contributors · 16 comments
  • Followers: 7
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

Drupal 12.0.0 ships with refreshed front-end libraries. jQuery goes from 4.0.0 to 4.1.0, htmx from 4.0.1 to 4.0.2, tabbable from 6.5.0 to 6.5.2 and transliteration from 2.6.1 to 2.7.0. The transliteration update fixes the mapping of Ý, which now becomes y instead of u when machine names are generated in the browser. If your custom or contrib JavaScript depends on jQuery or htmx internals, retest it against these versions.

Impact

Affects front-end developers and site owners.

  • Config change: Machine name transliteration now maps Ý to y instead of u, so generated machine names for input containing Ý differ.
  • Theme change: Bundled jQuery moves from 4.0.0 to 4.1.0 and htmx from 4.0.1 to 4.0.2; custom JS and themes relying on them should be retested.

Technical details

The vendored files under core/assets/vendor/ (jquery/jquery.min.js, htmx/htmx.min.js, tabbable/index.umd.min.js, transliteration/bundle.umd.min.js) were rebuilt, and the version and license URL entries for jquery, htmx, tabbable and transliteration in core/core.libraries.yml were updated to match core/package.json. The jQuery 4.1.0 diff includes Sizzle selector changes: simple tag and class selectors now go through querySelectorAll rather than getElementsByTagName and getElementsByClassName, and CSS escape handling and jQuery.uniqueSort were reworked. The htmx 4.0.2 diff changes how pending delayed or throttled triggers are cleared (scoped to the same hx-trigger value), <title> lookup in fragments, and the Firefox check for the Navigation API in history handling (now Firefox 159 and later).

Build-time dependencies were also bumped in core/package.json, including chokidar ^6, glob ^14, jsdom ^31, cspell, postcss-preset-env, prettier, webpack and webpack-cli. eslint, eslint-plugin-jsdoc and eslint-plugin-yml were deliberately not updated, and stylelint was kept at ^17.16.0 to match the 11.5.0 update (#3625623), with ESLint and PostCSS handled separately. The machine name FunctionalJavascript/Nightwatch test expectation changed from dnoooooxouuuuuthss to dnoooooxouuuuythss to reflect the transliteration fix.

  • Committed: November 21, 2026 (3 days later)

item.title: #3639248: Remove deprecated class properties
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 12.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +0/−60 · php +0/−60
  • Diff: 5570552
  • Discussion: #3639248 · 5 contributors · 14 comments
  • Followers: 5
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

Six core classes no longer carry deprecated service properties that used to be lazily resolved from the container with a deprecation notice. Code that extends these classes or reaches into those properties will no longer get the service and must obtain it another way. The removal was scheduled before the Drupal 12 release candidate.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Deprecated service properties removed: RouteBuilder::$controllerResolver and $moduleHandler, Router::$urlGenerator, ComponentNegotiator::$moduleExtensionList, Permission::$moduleHandler (views access), Permissions::$moduleHandler (views filter), AdminNegotiator::$entityTypeManager.

Technical details

These properties were deprecated through DeprecatedServicePropertyTrait and a $deprecatedProperties map, so they were missed when removals were found by grepping for deprecation strings. The issue also notes the trait hard-codes 11.0.0 as the removal version for properties, so the messages were wrong (see #3519400).

The commit removes the trait usage and the $deprecatedProperties arrays from Drupal\Core\Routing\RouteBuilder (controllerResolver => controller_resolver, moduleHandler => module_handler), Drupal\Core\Routing\Router (urlGenerator), Drupal\Core\Theme\ComponentNegotiator (moduleExtensionList), Drupal\user\Plugin\views\access\Permission and Drupal\user\Plugin\views\filter\Permissions (moduleHandler), and Drupal\user\Theme\AdminNegotiator (entityTypeManager). Two now-obsolete PHPStan baseline entries for DependencySerializationTrait private properties in Permission and Permissions were dropped. DirectoryWithMetadataDiscovery also uses the trait but was left out of scope, as its removal is scheduled for Drupal 13.

Upgrade

If a subclass or other code relied on these magic properties, inject the service explicitly, for example in a subclass of AdminNegotiator:

public function __construct(
  AccountInterface $user,
  protected EntityTypeManagerInterface $entityTypeManager,
  // ...
) {}

Same applies to moduleHandler on Permission/Permissions/RouteBuilder, urlGenerator on Router, and moduleExtensionList on ComponentNegotiator.

  • Opened: November 18, 2026
  • Committed: November 18, 2026

item.description:

  • Type: Critical task
  • Version: 12.0.x-dev

Summary

Drupal 12.0.x and main now ship Symfony 8.2.0-BETA2 (previously BETA1). The Symfony version constraints in core's Composer files were raised from 8.1 to 8.2. The release notes say Symfony will be updated again to stable 8.2.0 before Drupal 12.0.0 is released.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: Drupal core's composer.json and core/composer.json now require Symfony components ^8.2 instead of ^8.1; the lock file pins 8.2.0-BETA2 packages.

Technical details

The change is Composer-only: composer.json, core/composer.json and composer.lock were updated. The ^8.1 constraints for symfony/* packages (console, dependency-injection, event-dispatcher, filesystem, finder, http-foundation, http-kernel, mailer, mime, process, routing, runtime, serializer, validator, yaml, and dev packages such as browser-kit, css-selector, dom-crawler, error-handler, lock, var-dumper) became ^8.2. The issue thread says the constraints were bumped here because leaving them at ^8.1 after #3634655 (BETA1) caused failures in the Updated Dependencies CI job: Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route::__construct() received null for $alias when called from Drupal\Core\Routing\Attribute\Route. Some Symfony packages (css-selector, dom-crawler, error-handler, event-dispatcher, filesystem, process, psr-http-message-bridge, string, var-exporter) had no BETA2 release at the time. An unrelated Guzzle deprecation found in the same job was handled in #3638086.

item.title: #3634418: Implement better messaging for Assert for css in libraries discovery
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +15/−0 · php +9 · yml +6
  • Diff: 813e696
  • Discussion: #3634418 · 5 contributors · 12 comments
  • Followers: 6
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

If a CSS file in a *.libraries.yml file is listed without options (for example, a key with nothing after the colon instead of {}), the assertion error now says so. It reads: "CSS file options must be an array. Use {} when no options are needed." Before, the message said "CSS must be nested under a category," which pointed at the wrong problem. Assertions only run in development setups where assert() is enabled. The change was also backported to 11.5.x.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: LibraryDiscoveryParser::validateCssLibrary() now returns 3 when a CSS file entry has a NULL options value.

Technical details

LibraryDiscoveryParser::validateCssLibrary() now returns a new code 3 when a file's options value is NULL. YAML parses a key with no value as NULL, which previously failed the is_array() check and returned 1 (improper nesting). buildByExtension() has a new assertion that rejects code 3 and shows the new message. It runs before the existing < 2 and === 0 assertions, so the nesting message no longer masks it. The docblock return values list the new code. A kernel/unit test case Missing CSS options with a css_missing_options fixture covers it.

item.description:

Summary

Previously it stayed visible for every menu option, including No menu entry and the menu tab options, where it had no effect. This matches the other menu settings (title, description, parent, weight, context), which already hid when they did not apply.

A FunctionalJavascript test, testMenuExpandedVisibility(), was added to the views_ui tests. item.title: #3622391: Use tagged iterators in CacheTagsInvalidator
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 12.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +168/−21 · php +167/−17 · yml +1/−4
  • Diff: af2ff7c
  • Discussion: #3622391 · 7 contributors · 21 comments
  • Followers: 12
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 7 contributors

Summary

The cache tags invalidator no longer instantiates every cache tag invalidator service and every cache bin when it is built. They are loaded lazily, only when tags are actually invalidated. This removes a source of circular service references (for example a logger that reads config in its constructor, combined with a config override that triggers plugin discovery), and avoids constructing services that are never needed on a request. Sites or modules that subclass CacheTagsInvalidator or replace the cache_tags.invalidator service may need updating.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: cache_tags.invalidator service definition now uses !tagged_iterator arguments instead of service_collector tags.
  • API change: CacheTagsInvalidator has a new constructor taking iterable $invalidators, $bins and $memoryBins; the $invalidators and $bins properties are now iterable.

Technical details

The cache_tags.invalidator service in core.services.yml dropped the three service_collector tags (addInvalidator for cache_tags_invalidator, addBin for cache.bin and cache.bin.memory). It now passes !tagged_iterator cache_tags_invalidator, !tagged_iterator cache.bin and !tagged_iterator cache.bin.memory as constructor arguments. CacheTagsInvalidator gained a constructor with promoted protected iterable $invalidators = [], $bins = [] and $memoryBins = [].

item.title: #3623380: Create OOP replacement for hook_install_tasks and hook_install_tasks_alter
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +372/−21 · php +367/−21 · yml +5
  • Diff: 4f9558d
  • Discussion: #3623380 · 5 contributors · 33 comments
  • Followers: 8
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

Installation profiles can now provide their custom install tasks and task alterations through a class instead of hook_install_tasks() and hook_install_tasks_alter() in the .profile file. This removes one of the remaining reasons profiles need a procedural .profile file. The old procedural hooks still work but now trigger deprecation errors.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Procedural hook_install_tasks() and hook_install_tasks_alter() are deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and removed from drupal:13.0.0.
  • New API: New \Drupal\Core\Extension\Install\TasksInterface with getTasks(array &$install_state): array and alter(array &$tasks, array $install_state): void.

Technical details

A profile adds a class in src/Install/Tasks/ (namespace Drupal\PROFILE_NAME\Install\Tasks) that implements \Drupal\Core\Extension\Install\TasksInterface. getTasks(array &$install_state) replaces hook_install_tasks() and alter(array &$tasks, array $install_state) replaces hook_install_tasks_alter(). The class is created through \Drupal::classResolver(), so it can implement ContainerInjectionInterface. Only core services can safely be injected, because this runs before the install is complete.

In install.core.inc, install_tasks() calls the new install_get_tasks() and install_alter_tasks() helpers (both @internal). The procedural PROFILE_install_tasks() and PROFILE_install_tasks_alter() are only called when no OOP implementation supplied tasks (for getTasks) or exists (for alter). When the procedural fallback runs, it triggers an E_USER_DEPRECATED error pointing to https://www.drupal.org/node/3623397. The profile file is still loaded before alter(), so the class can rely on functions defined there.

The directory scan that install_check_class_requirements() used to find Install/Requirements classes was extracted into install_get_fixed_class_name(), which now serves both lookups. It require_onces each PHP file in the directory and keeps the class name of the last file it finds, so keep one class per Install/Tasks directory. The hook docs in core.api.php were updated with the @deprecated notes. Follow-up #3630429 is about changing the doc wording on state versus key value expirable.

Upgrade

Move the procedural hooks into a class, for example src/Install/Tasks/MyProfileTasks.php:

namespace Drupal\myprofile\Install\Tasks;

use Drupal\Core\Extension\Install\TasksInterface;

class MyProfileTasks implements TasksInterface {

  public function getTasks(array &$install_state): array {
    // Return what myprofile_install_tasks() returned.
    return [];
  }

  public function alter(array &$tasks, array $install_state): void {
    // Body of myprofile_install_tasks_alter().
  }

}

Then remove myprofile_install_tasks() and myprofile_install_tasks_alter() from the .profile file. If the class exists, the procedural versions are ignored.

item.title: #3273334: Unable to unselect a multi select exposed filter in ajax view
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +72/−7 · php +58/−5 · js +14/−2
  • Diff: 48f2609
  • Discussion: #3273334 · 13 contributors · 46 comments
  • Followers: 18
  • AI disclosures: 2 of 13 contributors

Summary

In an AJAX-enabled view with a multi-select exposed filter, you can now clear the selection. Previously, if the filter was already in the page URL (for example /admin/content?type[]=page), deselecting the value and pressing Filter re-selected it. The query string parameters for exposed filters are now correctly dropped before the AJAX request, so the submitted form values win. Query parameters in the resulting URLs can appear in a different order.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The bug was in core/modules/views/js/ajax_view.js. When building the AJAX request, the code removes existing exposed filter params from the page's query string, but it only matched input[name="..."] by exact name. select and textarea elements were never matched, and a multi-select named type[] did not match a URL param such as type[0] or type[]. A multi-select with nothing selected submits no value, so the stale URL param was passed through and re-applied.

The fix collects the base names of every [name] element in the exposed form into a Set, stripping any [...] suffix with a stripArraySuffix() helper. It then filters URL params by checking their suffix-stripped name against that set. This removes all exposed form fields from the URL, not only checkboxes and multi-selects, which can change the order of params in generated URLs. The committer noted this is closer to the original intent of the // Remove current exposed filters. comment. Existing FunctionalJavascript tests in the views and admin tests were updated for the new param order (for example title=Page%20Two&type=All&status=All). A new testUnselectMultiSelectExposedFilter covers clearing the selection and the type[0]/type[1] URL form. It was backported to 12.0.x, 11.x and 11.5.x.

item.title: #3635924: Upgrade htmx to 4.0.1
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 12.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +118/−98 · js +110/−90 · lock +5/−5 · yml +2/−2 · json +1/−1

Summary

Drupal core's bundled htmx JavaScript library is updated from 4.0.0 to 4.0.1. The issue says one fix in this release affects hx-partial, a new htmx 4 feature. The release also fixes other htmx behavior around request handling, triggers, out-of-band swaps and history. Sites and modules that build on core's HTMX support get the fixes automatically, with no code changes. The change was committed to main and 12.0.x.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The htmx library definition in core/core.libraries.yml now points to version 4.0.1, with the license URL updated to match. core/assets/vendor/htmx/htmx.min.js was regenerated, and package.json and yarn.lock pin htmx.org at 4.0.1. The unminified source diff shows these behavior changes:

  • hx-action, the verb attributes (hx-get, hx-post and so on), hx-trigger and hx-validate no longer pick up implicit inheritance from ancestors. #attributeValue gained an allowInheritance argument for this.
  • hx-trigger now accepts every 1s [cond]. The changed modifier is tracked per event target. A new trigger cancels any pending delayed or throttled trigger on the same element. intersect now observes the from: elements.
  • Boosted elements now go through #initializeTriggers.
  • Indicators and disabled elements are tracked on ctx.indicators and ctx.disabledElements. A request that is replaced no longer releases the queue slot of the request that replaced it. AbortError no longer fires htmx:error, except for timeouts. A swap is skipped if the target was removed while the request was in flight.
  • Out-of-band targets are resolved relative to the source element, and swapStyle:selector parsing was changed. The ignoreTitle swap modifier is now honored in more places. A scroll or show target of window or document is handled.
  • History is now stamped with replaceState on the first htmx swap rather than at initialization, and it is updated only after a swap is confirmed.
  • htmx.ajax() rejects with "Target not found" when an explicit target can't be resolved.
  • A named submit button that owns hx-post is treated as the submitter.
  • HTML is parsed with Document.parseHTMLUnsafe(trusted, {}) as a workaround for Chrome 150 to 156 dropping comments.

item.title: #3578936: Navigation module and Admin theme should use the same Inter font
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 25 files, +202/−94 · css +182/−74 · yml +20/−12 · php +0/−8
  • Diff: 3875e93
  • Discussion: #3578936 · 8 contributors · 46 comments
  • Followers: 12
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 8 contributors

Summary

Navigation and the Default Admin theme each used to load their own copy of the Inter font, so admin pages with both downloaded it twice (about 557 KB of fonts). Core now ships one shared Inter font, split by character set, and both use it. On a typical English admin page only the Latin subset (about 104 KB) is downloaded and preloaded. The issue's own Slow 4G measurements, which were generated with Claude, show fonts finishing loading about 2.6 seconds sooner. Default Admin moves from Inter v3 to v4, which Navigation already used, so admin headings come out a few percent narrower. Body text is almost unchanged.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Navigation and Default Admin no longer ship their own Inter @font-face CSS or font files; they depend on core/font. Admin typography now uses Inter v4, so headings render slightly narrower.
  • New API: New core/font library (Inter v4 variable, unicode-range subsets, preloaded latin file) and --drupal-font-inter CSS custom property.

Technical details

A new font library in core/core.libraries.yml loads core/misc/fonts/inter.css and preloads misc/fonts/inter-latin.woff2 through the library fonts key. inter.css declares eight @font-face blocks for the Inter family (latin, latin-ext, cyrillic, cyrillic-ext, greek, greek-ext, vietnamese, symbols), each with a unicode-range. Browsers fetch only the subsets needed by the characters on the page. The CSS also defines metric-adjusted fallback faces, Inter Fallback Helvetica Neue and Inter Fallback Arial, using size-adjust, ascent-override, descent-override and line-gap-override to reduce layout shift while Inter loads. :root gets --drupal-font-inter, which lists inter followed by those fallbacks and sans-serif. The --drupal- prefix was added after review to avoid clashing with other themes' variables. An unused --font-inter-size-adjust variable was removed.

Consumers now use the shared pieces. navigation/internal.navigation and default_admin/global-styling list core/font as a dependency, and their own fonts.css/font.css files, fonts: preload entries and (for Default Admin) the v3.19 font file reference are removed. --admin-toolbar-font-family in the Navigation variables and --admin-font-family in Default Admin are both set to var(--drupal-font-inter). The installer test assertion that the preloaded font URL avoids install.php was removed. Performance test expectations (StylesheetBytes) were updated. The change was also backported to 12.0.x, 11.x and 11.5.x.

Upgrade

Themes or modules that bundle their own Inter copy (for example Gin or Mercury, as discussed in the issue) can drop it and depend on the core library:

dependencies:
  - core/font

Then reference the shared stack in CSS:

--admin-font-family: var(--drupal-font-inter);

Custom CSS that depended on Navigation's or Default Admin's fonts.css/font.css files, or on their inter-var.woff2/inter.woff2 file paths, should switch to core/font.
